title: Conscious retry gate and tenant surge nurse to prevent retry amplification and preserve SLOs
creator: Priya Raman
description:
Summary:
During the latest tenant surge incidents we observed correlated increases in 5xxs and timeouts followed by aggressive client retries that amplified downstream load. This ticket designs and implements a "conscious retry gate" (CRG) and a per-tenant "surge nurse" that together limit retry amplification while preserving latency SLOs and fast recovery for healthy traffic.

Problem statement:
- Symptoms: tenant-scoped bursts cause short-lived host CPU / connection pressure, increasing transient 5xx/timeouts. Many clients immediately retry, producing repeated bursts and cascading failures.
- Impact: customer-visible errors and elevated latency across hosted and dedicated pools, escalations from 3 enterprise customers during last 72h.
- Existing mitigations (circuit breakers, global backoff) are too coarse — they either cut healthy traffic or fail to stop repeated client retries quickly.

Root-cause hypothesis:
1) Short-lived slowpath conditions (cold KV cache shred, kernel contention during warm-start) produce 5xx spikes that recover in <30s.
2) Client SDKs and integrators aggressively retry without tenant-scoped hysteresis or budget awareness.
3) Proxy/admission layers do not surface per-tenant retry budgets to clients or downstream admission.

Design goals:
- Stop retry amplification during short spikes while avoiding over-throttling steady traffic.
- Provide transparent signals for SDKs and customers (retry-budget headers + Console view).
- Apply minimally invasive controls for Dedicated/Private: prefer configurable guardrails (opt-in for Private but default-on for Hosted).

Proposed solution (high-level):
1) Conscious Retry Gate (CRG): per-tenant state machine that maintains a short sliding window of recent error-rate, average latency, and in-flight count. When transient signals exceed thresholds, CRG returns a small set of defensive responses for new requests: HTTP 429 with Retry-After; 202 accept-with-defer token; or an idempotent fast-fail with a structured error payload advising exponential backoff. CRG is implemented at the edge/admission proxy so it protects both hosted and routed dedicated pools.

2) Tenant Surge Nurse: a lightweight admission controller per-tenant that allocates a retry budget and gradual reintroduction policy. It keeps a token bucket for allowed retries, decays allowance faster for tenants causing system pressure, and issues short-lived "grace tokens" to high-priority customers. The surge nurse collaborates with CRG via headers that carry: current_retry_budget, in_flight_hint, and short-term_slowpath_flag.

3) SDK and Console integration: update official SDKs to honour Retry-After and budget headers. Console will show a new per-tenant "Retry Health" panel (and an API endpoint) which surfaces budget, last-surge events, and recommended client-side backoff knobs.

4) Observability and telemetry:
- New metrics: tenant_retry_budget_remaining, tenant_surge_events{severity}, crg_actions{drop,slowfail,accept-defer}, per-tenant p99 latency pre/post CRG.
- Dashboards: surge timeline + customer-impact table, and a golden signal alert that triggers SRE paging when a tenant causes sustained budget depletion across multiple hosts.

5) Safe rollout plan:
A) Canary run on internal tenants -> capture metrics and false-positive rate.
B) Opt-in beta for 10 customers (hosted) plus one Dedicated customer to validate config knobs.
C) Gradual default-on for Hosted after 2-week soak with rollback gates. Private customers may opt-in; we provide an on-prem connector and configuration guide.

Implementation notes / trade-offs:
- CRG lives in the admission proxy codepath (low-latency C++ path). To avoid per-request persistent storage we keep a small in-memory LRU for active tenants and persist slowly to a distributed state for long-lived signals. This trades memory for low-latency protection.
- Because we modify upstream responses (429/202 structured payloads), we must update SDKs and publish clear migration guidance; otherwise some clients may misinterpret 202 as permanent accept.
- We avoid immediate hard circuits; instead prefer soft fencing to allow important traffic (priority customers) through with grace tokens.

Testing and validation:
- Unit tests for CRG state transitions and surge nurse token semantics.
- Integration tests simulating tenant burst patterns (synthetic load with varied retry patterns) verifying the system reduces p95 token cost and converges without starving healthy requests.
- Chaos runbook simulating failed CRG host and verifying cascade prevention.

Rollout / rollback criteria:
- Proceed to broad rollout if canary shows >=60% reduction in retry amplification without >2% increase in 5xx for non-impacted tenants.
- Rollback immediately if any of: unexpected global latency regression >10% p99, sustained increase in customer errors >5% across >=3 tenants, or a CRG bug causes incorrect retry header injection for >10% of requests.

Customer communication:
- Drafted template in drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1n-ReDwood/tenant-surge-notify (internal).
- Messaging: explain short-term automated protection, how to opt-out, SDK updates, and expected behaviour (Retry-After vs transient 5xx).

Links:
- Incident chronology + learning doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/2024-11-tenant-surge-postmortem
- Design diagram: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1CRG-design-diagram
- Prototype PR (edge proxy): https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/12456

Open follow-ups:
- Add per-tenant regression monitoring tied to eval prompt sets (reduce false positives for workloads sensitive to 202-style responses).
- Quantize CRG memory footprint and add a low-memory mode for Private deployments.
- Legal review for response payload changes for regulated customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- CRG active in canary region, telemetry emitting for all new metrics, SDKs updated to respect Retry-After semantics, and no customer-visible regressions after 2-week soak in canary.
comments: 2024-11-06 - Priya Raman: Ticket created after SEV escalations from three customers. Added initial design and goals.

2024-11-07 - Liam Soto: Spike session notes - we validated in local harness that soft-429 reduces downstream retries by ~72% in synthetic tests. Edge PR skeleton landed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/edge-proxy/pull/12456
2024-11-08 - Aisha Kaur (SRE): Observability plan added. Suggest adding an ephemeral per-tenant trace id to link client retry waves to infra signals.
2024-11-09 - Design review (Jonah Beck): Approve concept, request to add 'grace token' TTL to avoid long-lived bypasses. See design comments in Confluence.
2024-11-11 - QA (Marina Ortiz): Integration tests failing intermittently in low-memory mode; investigating LRU eviction timing as possible cause.
2024-11-12 - Legal (Daniel Cho): Flagged for review for Private customers that may need explicit consent before response semantics change. Added as follow-up.

2024-11-14 - Liam Soto: Canary rollout started for internal tenants in us-west-2. Initial telemetry: tenant_retry_budget_remaining decreased for stressed tenants, aggregate p95 CPU unchanged. Observed one false-positive on a high-priority tenant; issued immediate grace token and tracking sub-issue ENG-861000.

2024-11-15 - Priya Raman: Updated rollout plan to include a 'silent' mode that emits headers but does not change response code for the first 48h of external beta to monitor client behaviours before enforcing 429/202 behaviours.
